05 · Python NLP

Use different libraries for different jobs

Practical rule: NLTK can tokenize, spaCy extracts entities, and Transformers can classify sentiment. Always test on labeled examples.

# pip install nltk spacy transformers torch scikit-learn
# python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm
from nltk.tokenize import wordpunct_tokenize
import spacy
from transformers import pipeline
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score

text = "Ravi works at OpenAI in Hyderabad."
tokens = wordpunct_tokenize(text)
doc = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")(text)
entities = [(e.text, e.label_) for e in doc.ents]
sentiment = pipeline(
    "sentiment-analysis",
    model="distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
)
items = ["I loved it!", "It was disappointing."]
gold = ["POSITIVE", "NEGATIVE"]
pred = [sentiment(t)[0]["label"] for t in items]
print(tokens, entities, accuracy_score(gold, pred))
How to test

First install the packages and download the English spaCy model. Transformers will fetch pretrained weights on first use.

Accuracy: Compare predictions with trusted labels on a held-out test set.

*The depicted entity labels are illustrative, not verified outputs.

This example uses English models; evaluate other languages separately.

06 · Modern NLP models

BERT reads context, T5 transforms text, GPT continues text

Easy distinction: BERT looks across an input, T5 reads and writes text, and GPT predicts the next token.
